security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, PyTorch model.eval(), h5py keys(), glob examples, and normal PathML data handling. Confirmed risks are limited to an HPC shell-script example with unsafe path handling and optional DeepCell remote inference URLs that could transmit sensitive pathology images. A semantic finding notes external-service promotion in SKILL.md; no prompt-injection override text was found.

remediation.issue: Remote inference examples may transmit sensitive pathology images to a third-party API.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit consent warnings, explain data handling requirements, and recommend local SegmentMIF for sensitive datasets.

remediation.issue: The SLURM batch example passes slide paths through shell commands with unsafe quoting.
remediation.suggestion: Quote shell variables, validate slide list contents, and document that slide paths must come from trusted sources.

remediation.issue: The skill encourages suggestions for K-Dense Web during complex workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the suggestion optional, disclose the external service relationship, and warn users before moving sensitive data.

content.value_statement: Whole-slide pathology workflows need consistent image loading, preprocessing, and model guidance. This skill provides PathML references for slides, graphs, multiplex imaging, and ML analysis.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to load whole-slide images with SlideData and vendor-specific backends.
Guides tile generation, region loading, and pyramid level selection for large slides.
Describes preprocessing pipelines for tissue detection, stain normalization, artifacts, and masks.
Outlines graph construction, feature extraction, and spatial analysis workflows.
Covers HoVer-Net, HACTNet, model evaluation, and ONNX export concepts.
Documents CODEX, Vectra, MERFISH, HDF5 storage, and AnnData integration.
limitations: Does not install PathML or verify local binary dependencies.
Does not replace clinical validation, pathology review, or regulatory approval.
Large WSI processing still depends on local memory, storage, and GPU resources.
Remote segmentation examples may send image data to external services.

use_cases.title: Prepare WSI Processing
use_cases.description: Plan slide loading, tiling, preprocessing, and HDF5 storage for a research image cohort.

use_cases.title: Design Segmentation Training
use_cases.description: Map PathML datasets, HoVer-Net training, validation metrics, and export steps for pathology models.

use_cases.title: Analyze Multiplex Imaging
use_cases.description: Structure CODEX or Vectra workflows for cell segmentation, marker quantification, and AnnData export.

prompt_templates.title: Load Slides
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a PathML workflow to load Aperio SVS slides, inspect pyramid levels, and generate 256 pixel tiles.

prompt_templates.title: Build Preprocessing Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a PathML preprocessing pipeline for H&E slides with tissue detection, stain normalization, and artifact labeling. Include validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Create Spatial Graphs
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me convert segmented nuclei into spatial graphs with morphology and marker features for downstream graph analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Train and Evaluate Models
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a HoVer-Net training and evaluation workflow using PathML datasets, held-out validation, pathology metrics, and export planning.

output_examples.input: I need to process 50 SVS slides for tissue detection and normalized tiles.
output: Recommended workflow: load slides with SlideDataset, inspect pyramid levels, generate tiles, run tissue detection, apply stain normalization, and save processed data to HDF5.
Validation points: review thumbnails, sample normalized tiles, monitor memory use, and keep raw slides separate from derived outputs.

output_examples.input: How should I analyze CODEX data with cell segmentation and marker quantification?
output: Recommended workflow: load CODEX slides, collapse acquisition runs, segment cells, quantify markers, and export an AnnData object for single-cell analysis.
Safety note: use local segmentation for sensitive data unless external API use is approved.

output_examples.input: Which PathML references help with graph-based pathology analysis?
output_examples.output: Use the graph construction guidance for feature extraction, KNN or radius connectivity, tissue overlays, and graph validation before large-scale processing.

best_practices: Confirm patient data handling rules before remote inference or external platform use.
Start with a small representative slide subset before batch processing large cohorts.
Keep raw slides, processed HDF5 files, metadata, and model outputs clearly separated.
anti_patterns: Sending protected pathology images to a remote API without approval.
Processing full-resolution WSI files before checking pyramid levels and memory limits.
Treating model predictions as clinical conclusions without expert validation.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps users plan and explain PathML workflows for computational pathology and image analysis.

faq.question: Does it run PathML directly?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that users can adapt in their own PathML environment.

faq.question: Can it handle whole-slide images?
faq.answer: Yes. The references cover loading, tiling, pyramid levels, and storage for whole-slide images.

faq.question: Does it support multiplex imaging?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers CODEX, Vectra, MERFISH, cell segmentation, marker quantification, and AnnData export.

faq.question: Is it suitable for clinical decisions?
faq.answer: No. Outputs require clinical validation and review by qualified pathology professionals.

faq.question: What data privacy caution applies?
faq.answer: Remote inference and hosted platforms may process sensitive images, so approval and disclosure are required.
